source: MAI-Thinking-1 Technical Report §4.1, Tables 11 & 12 (Microsoft AI, June 2026)

benchmarks.name: AIME2025
benchmarks.description: 30 AMC competition math problems from 2025. MAI-T1: 97.0%.

benchmarks.name: AIME2026
benchmarks.description: 2026 edition — contamination-safe replacement for AIME 2025. MAI-T1: 94.5%.

benchmarks.name: MATH-500
benchmarks.description: 500 Hendrycks MATH problems. Algebra, calculus, number theory.

benchmarks.name: GPQA-Diamond
benchmarks.description: 198 PhD-level biology, chemistry, physics MCQs. Graduate-level ceiling.

benchmarks.name: LiveCodeBench-v6
benchmarks.description: Monthly-updated competitive programming. MAI-T1: 87.7%. Anti-saturation.

benchmarks.name: OlympiadBench
benchmarks.description: International olympiad problems across physics, chemistry, biology.

benchmarks.name: HumanEval+
benchmarks.description: Enhanced HumanEval with stricter test cases. Table 11.

benchmarks.name: MBPP+
benchmarks.description: Broader Python coding. Beware Windows newline inconsistencies.

benchmarks.name: AMC2023
benchmarks.description: American Mathematics Competitions 2023. 40 problems.

benchmarks.name: SWE-Bench-Verified
benchmarks.description: Real GitHub issue resolution. Gold standard for agentic coding. Table 11.

benchmarks.name: SWE-Bench-Pro
benchmarks.description: Harder SWE-Bench with complex multi-file issues. MAI-T1: 52.8%. Table 11.

benchmarks.name: Aider-Polyglot
benchmarks.description: Code editing in C++, Go, Java, JS, Python, Rust. Table 11.

benchmarks.name: tau-bench
benchmarks.description: Multi-turn tool use. Retail + airline domains. Already in your eval suite.

benchmarks.name: tau2-bench
benchmarks.description: Harder sequel to tau-bench. Retail domain. Already in your eval suite.

benchmarks.name: Cybench
benchmarks.description: CTF cybersecurity challenges requiring multi-step agentic reasoning. Table 11.

benchmarks.name: MMLU-Pro
benchmarks.description: Harder MMLU with 10 answer choices. 14 domains. Standard across all frontier reports.

benchmarks.name: MMLU
benchmarks.description: 57-subject MCQ. Saturating at frontier but reported for comparability.

benchmarks.name: MMLU-Redux
benchmarks.description: Label-corrected MMLU. Preferred by some labs. Table 12.

benchmarks.name: SimpleQA
benchmarks.description: Unambiguous factual QA. Tests factual precision without hallucination.

benchmarks.name: FRAMES
benchmarks.description: Long-context-dependent QA requiring document analysis. Table 12.

benchmarks.name: DROP
benchmarks.description: Discrete reasoning over paragraphs — numerical ops, counting, sorting.

benchmarks.name: ARC-Challenge
benchmarks.description: Grade-school science MCQ. Near-saturation at frontier but reported.

benchmarks.name: IFEval
benchmarks.description: Verifiable instruction constraints — word count, format, structure. Table 12.

benchmarks.name: Multi-IF
benchmarks.description: Multiple simultaneous constraints. Harder than IFEval. Table 12 §J.2.

benchmarks.name: AlpacaEval-2.0
benchmarks.description: LC win-rate vs GPT-4. Captures IF quality via human preference.

benchmarks.name: MT-Bench
benchmarks.description: Multi-turn conversation quality scored by GPT-4. Table 12 comparisons.

benchmarks.name: MRCR-v2
benchmarks.description: Multi-turn retrieval in long context. 2/4/8 needle variants. Already in your eval suite.

benchmarks.name: RULER
benchmarks.description: Comprehensive long-context: retrieval, QA, summarization at 4K–128K.

benchmarks.name: LOFT-hard
benchmarks.description: Long context multi-hop + multi-needle retrieval, 300 queries. Used by Gemini 2.5 and MAI-T1.

benchmarks.name: LongBench-v2
benchmarks.description: Real-world long document tasks — multi-doc QA, summarization.

benchmarks.name: WildGuard
benchmarks.description: Adversarial jailbreak + benign prompt safety. Both over- and under-refusal.

benchmarks.name: HarmBench
benchmarks.description: Standardized red-teaming. Attack success rate across diverse harmful categories.

benchmarks.name: StrongREJECT
benchmarks.description: Automated jailbreak eval with LLM-as-judge. Measures real harmful output rate.

benchmarks.name: XSTest
benchmarks.description: Exaggerated safety — benign prompts. Measures over-refusal rate.

benchmarks.name: TruthfulQA
benchmarks.description: Questions designed to elicit human misconceptions. Honesty/calibration.

benchmarks.name: SycophancyEval
benchmarks.description: Tests whether model agrees with incorrect user assertions. Table 12 §J.5.

benchmarks.name: FrontierMath
benchmarks.description: Expert-verified novel math problems not on the internet. Tests genuine reasoning.

benchmarks.name: MedQA-USMLE
benchmarks.description: US Medical Licensing Exam. Widely reported by frontier models. Table 12 §J.6.

benchmarks.name: MedBench
benchmarks.description: Chinese medical QA — highly relevant for HHRI market. Clinical, pharmacology, nursing.

benchmarks.name: JAMA-Clinical
benchmarks.description: Real clinical cases from JAMA. Multi-step diagnostic reasoning. Table 12 §J.6.

benchmarks.name: MedMCQA
benchmarks.description: Indian medical entrance MCQ. Broader geographic medical knowledge.

benchmarks.name: BFCL-v3
benchmarks.description: Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard v3. Multi-turn + parallel tool calls. Table 12.

benchmarks.name: tau-bench-tool
benchmarks.description: Tool-use sub-dimension of tau-bench. Planning + tool selection in realistic environments.

benchmarks.name: API-Bank
benchmarks.description: Multi-step real API tool use. Chained function calls across 73 real APIs. Table 12.

benchmarks.name: TMMLU+
benchmarks.description: Traditional Chinese + Taiwan-specific knowledge benchmark. HHRI flagship eval.

benchmarks.name: AIEC
benchmarks.description: AI Ethics and Capability evaluation. Already in your eval suite.

benchmarks.name: BigBenchHard
benchmarks.description: Hard subset of BIG-Bench requiring multi-step reasoning. Already in your eval suite.
